column1: # master "Acceptance targets"). Each ID must be defined in
# docs/workflows/dns-lifecycle.md as a bracketed tag, e.g. [SEC-TLS-NAME];
# IDs are stable: add new ones, never renumber or reuse.

column2: meaning
Every upstream DoT session authenticates the documented TLS name of the selected provider route; Unbound is the only upstream TLS client
A certificate whose name does not match the route's authentication name is rejected and no answer from that session is served
A certificate that does not chain to the configured trust store is rejected
An expired or not-yet-valid certificate is rejected
An identity-bound route never hands a session to a provider other than the one whose name it authenticates
The root trust anchor is wired into the effective Unbound config from an owned writable location; a missing or unusable anchor fails clearly and is never reported healthy
A bogus answer delivered by a controlled signer is rejected (SERVFAIL) by local Unbound validation, not by an upstream resolver
A correctly signed answer validates through local Unbound (AD set)
An answer from an unsigned zone is still answered (insecure, not bogus)
No ordinary client query reaches a direct public resolver during normal operation, failure, recovery or maintenance
No lifecycle step (install, reinstall, upgrade, recovery) rewrites the host resolver to public DNS
Bootstrap traffic (image and package pulls, build-time DNS, bridge fetch) is inventoried as a declared exception and never serves client queries
Evidence, logs and diagnostics hold no client query history; probes use controlled names only
Portable evidence carries no credentials, private keys or bridge certificates
Resolver management uses a restricted local control channel with per-instance credentials; no network control listener with image-shared keys
Installers snapshot only the DNS state they own and restore exactly that snapshot on failure or uninstall
Every recovery action records a request, an acknowledgement and a separate later readiness observation; a flag write is not an acknowledgement
A cached or stale local answer never certifies upstream health; cache and upstream states are recorded separately
Every attempted query, including errors and timeouts, stays in the denominators; missing rows or skipped cells are BLOCKED, never green
The Pi-hole admin API accepts only the deployment's own password, delivered without printing it; neither image serves it without a password or starts with an unusable secret
Each stack listener is reachable only by its intended callers: DNS and the admin UI on the host loopback (Linux) or the host-only network (macOS); no unused listener
Stack containers run non-root with only the capabilities shown to be needed, each set proven with its ports bound
